claim: Lessons in the catalog come from rules that ran in a real project, with the evidence they carry; /morph-update offers matching ones and /morph-share sends yours back.
note: The checker requires an evidence field on every lesson, and scripts/lesson-stats.sh counts the lessons with no fired count for the README. Whether a lesson's evidence is true is a maintainer's call at review.

claim: A change that alters behaviour gets a plan with testable acceptance criteria that the owner approves before code is written (short off the risk paths, full on them); a small bug fix starts from a failing test and a change with no behaviour change has no plan.

proofs.contains: obtain human approval on the plan before any implementation
The human approves it as any plan

note: A rule the Technical Lead reads before every full or bug plan (AGENTS.md, which every session loads, sends it there). Nothing in the self-test runs a model, so following it is not measured.

claim: Every change records the checks it ran with their exit codes, and a planned change the evidence for each criterion; a separate QA agent runs only in full and bug mode.
note: The record templates and the merge gate that requires them are checked on every render; whether a session fills them is not.

claim: Retros turn real misses into rules, and prunes propose cutting, merging or moving out rules that never fire, each cut approved by the owner.
note: The prune counter runs in the self-test on fresh and filled installs (the count, a due prune, the size budgets). The retro and the prune audit are written by the model and every cut is the owner's call; nothing replays them, so the claim rests on the kit's text.

claim: The guard blocks protected-branch pushes, force-pushes, secret files, a bare env, known remote database writes and changes that would switch it off; asks before deploys, publishes, merges and connector writes; blocks the call when it can't run its check.
note: Every case replays in the self-test, on every sample project when the guard or its cases change; the "git status" proofs include the cases that run with python3 or the guard's config missing. Cases call the script directly, not through Claude Code; the hook's own wiring is tested by a run with the script missing and one with git hanging. It stops accidents, not intent: tests/known-gaps.md lists what it does not see.

claim: Every change to the kit's template, update notes or tests runs a self-test that installs it into sample projects, replays the guard's cases and brings the previous release up to date.
note: The selftest workflow runs on changes to the template, update notes, the update skill, the tests and the README; changes to other skills, lessons and profiles don't trigger it. At every release tag, release.yml runs the report at the tag and fails unless the page names that tag's commit and release from a clean checkout.

claim: Each hand-off ends with an estimated dollar cost from Claude Code's own transcripts, split by agent.
note: The self-test runs the script on a project with no transcripts, on transcripts with subagents, a budget, torn and badly typed lines and a resumed session, and checks the Cost and budget lines it prints. The split by agent reads Claude Code's per-agent transcripts, and no case checks that split. Whether the Technical Lead pastes the line is not checked, nor is pricing against a real bill, which is why the README calls it an estimate.

claim: Branches, environments, checks, modules, risk areas, models, effort and loop limits live in one harness.config.yml; every rule and checklist is a plain Markdown file.
note: Every config key must be documented and every documented key must exist; each module can be added and removed.

claim: New or existing repos, monorepos, folders that aren't a git repo, any language or framework.
note: Closest measurable proxy: the kit renders and checks clean on four sample projects (Go, Python, a monorepo, Next.js). Not covered: other stacks, a repo with its own agent setup, and a folder with no git.

claim: Not a sandbox, doesn't make the model smarter; a full-mode feature costs several times a plain session, so only risky changes get the agents and clear small requests use a lean path.
note: The limits are stated and the lean path is documented; how much it saves in a session is not measured.

claim: Paste one prompt into Claude Code and the agent installs the harness by following INSTALL.md.

proofs.contains: Ask the user before anything that leaves the repo

note: Whether the install is easy is a human judgement. Proxy: the render and its self-checks run on four sample projects. Not covered: the conversation itself.

claim: Adding the marketplace and installing the plugin gives the /morph-* skills.
note: The manifests are checked for the plugin name; the real marketplace install is done by hand at release.

claim: scripts/install.sh copies the kit into a repo and never overwrites.

proofs.contains: install.sh never overwrote or chmodded a user file

note: The self-test runs install.sh into an empty folder, a copy that stops half way, and repos with their own settings.json, guard.sh, an ignored .claude/ and a linked AGENTS.md, and checks that no existing file changed.

claim: Needs bash, git, python3 3.7 or later, awk and perl, checked by /morph-doctor; small mode costs more than a plain session and full mode several times as much; every hand-off ends with a Cost line.
note: The doctor skill names every tool the README lists, and each session start checks python3; the doctor's checks are run by the model, not replayed. The cost comparison with a plain session comes from runs made by hand, not from a test.
